newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 28.

text.p: FINANCIAL TIMES
BP TO EXPAND IN ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA

It is reported that British Petroleum is looking to Asia and Latin America for the major part of its planned international expansion over the next 10 years. Over the forthcoming five years the company is hoping to achieve double digit growth in these markets. Should the growth targets be met Asia and Latin America could by the end of the decade account for 25 per cent of the company's revenues.
LABOUR MAY DELAY EMU ENTRY

The shadow foreign secretary Robin Cook has admitted that should Labour form the next government it would have difficulty taking the country into a single currency and that this move might have to be delayed until after the following election in the year 2002. This is noted to have been the most hard-headed assessment to date from Labour of the prospects for UK participation in Emu. Cook noted that the party might be concerned about shaping economic policy purely to meet Maastricht criteria.
SOCGEN MAY SELL EQUITY AND PROPERTY ASSETS

It is reported that the French banking group Societe Generale is considering embarking on a disposal of a large proportion of its equity and property portfolio. Such a move would provide the bank with considerable capital gains. UK investors in the bank are reported to be concerned that the current assets held in these fields are too large for a bank.
UK FAILING TO CLOSE NORTH-SOUTH WEALTH GAP, REPORTS SAYS

According to an EU review of regional policy the British government is failing to gap the divide in wealth terms that exists between the north and the south of the country. The conclusions of the report are seen as potentially an indictment of government economic policy and claims that it has allowed all sections of society to reap benefits. On a broader level the EU report found that the gap in wealth between the north and the south of Europe as a whole is diminishing.
ALLIANCE FLOAT TO GIVE SAVERS 1,000 STG IN SHARES

Next year's planned flotation of the Alliance & Leicester building society will result in those with savings receiving 250 shares apiece, worth in the region of one thousand stg. The 3.2 million savers will on Monday receive details of the planned flotation. The Halifax and Woolwich building societies are also planning to convert to bank status at some point in 1997. Those with the Alliance hoping to benefit will have to have opened their accounts prior to the end of December 1995.
SFA CHIEF URGES REFORM OF FINANCIAL SUPERVISION

The head of the Securities and Futures Authority, Richard Farrant, has called for the creation of a single body with responsibility for overseeing the regulation of banks, fund managers and investment banks. Speaking privately he expressed concern that the current regulatory framework is becoming antiquated. His comments come in advance of a report which will call for the supervision of banking to be removed from the Bank of England.
EU SET TO CLOSE VAT LOOPHOLE FOR OVERSEAS TELECOM GROUPS

Changes are planned by the European Union that will remove a loophole which allows foreign telecommunications companies operating in Europe to avoid having to charge Value added tax, enabling them to under-price local rivals. At present companies not registered in the EU are able to avoid applying this tax to services. The changes have been demanded by Britain, but backed by taxation authorities in other EU member states.
EMU "COULD COST BANKS 5 BILLION DOLLARS'

A report from the Boston Consulting Group has warned that the implantation of a single European currency could cost banks as much as 5 billion dollars in terms of lost revenues. Emu could deal a major blow to the ability of EU banks to compete internationally in terms of global cross-border payment transmissions. Already the BCG notes that customers are applying pressure for the costs of transferring money internationally to be reduced.
EUROPE'S IT MARKET SET FOR FURTHER RAPID GROWTH

According to the Information Technology Observatory there will be an increase of 8 per cent in the European market for IT and telecoms services and technology. Much of this demand will be seen in the outsourcing of IT functions, demand for higher performance computer hardware and increasing use of telecommunications systems. This year, however, the ITO has admitted demand will be less than had previously been anticipated, at a revised 6.6 per cent.
"EMU RUSH MAY HARM SINGLE CURRENCY'

The National Institute of Economic and Social Research will on Monday warn that the rush to create the planned single European on January 1 1999 risks harming the process from the outset. The institute notes that such is the rush to prepare for the euro that wrong decisions may well be made and important issues overlooked. Note is also made of the possibility that a lax interpretation of the Maastricht criteria could allow some countries to qualify for participation before they are actually ready.
